title: The first turban
hook: a ceremony when a young person ties the full turban for the first time
tomorrow: a teammate asks Simran: is Sikhi yours, or your parents'?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Bebe's three words, nobody knows that, then what she did know: honest answers. Today's question has an answer. It's just a strange one.

Graduations hand you a cap. Some teams hand a new player a jersey at a little ceremony. Gurveer, fifteen, from Simran's kirtan class, is getting something stranger: a long length of cloth, starched and folded, and a whole Sunday program built around him tying it. Simran's dad, Harjit, calls it the day Gurveer gets crowned. Here's the odd part. A crown is something somebody else puts on your head, once, and it's made of gold. This one is cotton. And Gurveer has to put it on himself.
screen: `A CAP, A JERSEY.` → `A LENGTH OF STARCHED CLOTH.` → `WHY CALL COTTON A CROWN?`

segments.voice: The ceremony is dastar bandi: dastar, the turban, and bandi, tying. Families hold it at the gurdwara, before the Guru Granth Sahib, with Ardas and a hukam, and sometimes an elder helps tie the first one. Some young women and girls tie a dastar too. Here's something to tell a friend tonight. The turban isn't one of the five Ks. Kesh, the uncut hair, is. The dastar is what covers and keeps the kesh, and the Sikh code asks Sikh men to wear one. So why a crown? Some Sikhs point to a line on ang 1084, in a hymn by Guru Arjan, that pairs a whole, uncut form, sabat soorat, with the dastar on the head, as part of a life given to God. And tradition says that in the Gurus' time, a turban marked people of rank. The Gurus' Sikhs wore it whoever they were. Which solves the puzzle. A king is crowned once, by someone above him. A Sikh ties this crown with their own hands, again every morning, with no one above them but the Guru. It's dignity you put on yourself, as a promise. Gurveer gets it a little crooked the first time. Harjit says his own was worse.
screen: `DASTAR BANDI: TYING THE TURBAN.` · `NOT A K: IT KEEPS THE KESH.` · `ANG 1084: SABAT SOORAT, DASTAR.` · `A CROWN YOU TIE YOURSELF, DAILY.` · then, large: `CROWNED.`

segments.voice: Find a scarf, a dish towel, or any long cloth. Fold it lengthwise into a neat, even band, smoothing each fold with your palm, and tie it once, carefully, around your wrist or your knee. Then let your hands rest and keep the feel of that care for the sit.
Dastar bandi. The ceremony where a young Sikh ties the full turban for the first time, before the Guru.
Crowned: by your own hands, every single morning, and a little crooked at first. That's today.
